5788.title: Fix docs/Pages deployment for the existing Uno 7 WASM layout
5788.body:
* Fix Pages deploy for the Uno 7 WASM publish layout (#5771)

Uno.Sdk 7 ships Uno.Wasm.Bootstrap 10, which writes uno-config.js at the
wwwroot root instead of package_<hash>/, adds root-absolute references to it
in index.html and service-worker.js, and sets WEBAPP_PATH = '/' in the
service worker. The smoke scripts still required package_*/uno-config.js, so
every Pages - Deploy run on main has failed since #5377, and the
Assemble site rewrite no longer covered the new absolute paths.

Publish the Gallery and SkiaFiddle with WasmShellWebAppBasePath=./ so every
bootstrapper-generated path is relative, and make the Gallery manifest's
start_url and scope relative. The copies then work at /gallery-uno/,
/fiddle/ and the staging prefixes without post-publish rewriting, so drop the sed rewrite from Assemble site.
Each Uno app job instead checks that no root-absolute reference reappears;
a violation fails that app, which the site then omits like any other
failed app, so docs still publish.

Update both smoke scripts to check the Uno 7 layout and to serve the app
from a sub-path, so a root-absolute reference fails the smoke test instead
of only breaking the deployed site. Exempt the bootstrapper's handled
only-if-cached probe (net::ERR_CACHE_MISS) in both drivers, matching the
existing exemption in BrowserRunningApp.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pin Pages app validation to Playwright-supported Ubuntu 24.04

The existing smoke-test Playwright version cannot install Chromium on ubuntu-latest now that it resolves to Ubuntu 26.04. Keep the existing dependencies and run the Pages app jobs on Ubuntu 24.04 instead.

5649.title: [iOS/tvOS] Build device frameworks from device archives
5649.body:
[iOS/tvOS] Build device frameworks from device archives (#5649)

Fixes: #5648

Keep device and simulator frameworks tied to their matching Apple archives,
so device packages carry device binaries and metadata without losing simulator
support.

~~ Simulator slices in device frameworks ~~

The iOS and tvOS build scripts copied the x86_64 simulator archive beside the
arm64 device archive. `CreateFatFramework` then combined the binaries and
copied the framework metadata from the simulator archive. Consequently,
device frameworks contained a simulator slice and declared
`iPhoneSimulator` or `AppleTVSimulator`; apps embedding them as-is could fail
App Store validation with ITMS-90087.

Build the device frameworks from the device archive alone and omit the
x86_64 device dSYM entries for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp. Keep the
simulator frameworks and symbols, including their x86_64 and arm64 slices.
Update `Get-AppleArtifacts` to expect arm64 for iOS and tvOS device outputs;
macOS, Mac Catalyst, and simulator expectations remain unchanged.

Downloaded-package inspection confirmed the device and simulator slices and
platform metadata for both libraries. Consumer builds passed for the six
iOS/tvOS device and simulator RIDs. An iOS simulator app used both libraries
successfully (`pixel=#ffff0000`, `skia=158.0`, `glyphs=2339`); tvOS was
build-validated. The PR's CI checks passed.

~~ x64-only native builds ~~

When `--arch=x64` skips the arm64 device archive, the previous unconditional
device-framework creation passes an empty archive list to `CreateFatFramework`
and fails before simulator output is produced. Guard device-framework creation
on arm64 not being skipped, while leaving simulator-framework creation
unconditional. Clean HarfBuzzSharp iOS and tvOS builds verified x64-only,
arm64-only, and all-architecture outputs.

Co-authored-by: Matteo Muratore <matteomuratoredev@gmail.com>

5760.title: Add the SKMesh API (custom vertex-mesh drawing)
5760.body:
Add the SKMesh API (custom vertex-mesh drawing) (#5760)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3777
Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/456
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4553
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/3779
Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/297
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/1c8b6db33a5c9ff2292fb58d65d7b344e91085f3...5d226f638edbb3c0dac0ac93ac1ff349298880a4

Expose Skia's custom vertex-mesh pipeline in SkiaSharp through
SKMeshSpecification, SKMeshSpecificationAttribute, SKMeshSpecificationVarying,
SKMeshSpecificationBuilder, SKMesh, SKMeshBuilder, SKIndexedMeshBuilder,
SKMeshVertexBuffer, SKMeshIndexBuffer, and SKCanvas.DrawMesh, while advancing
externals/skia and cgmanifest.json to 5d226f638edbb3c0dac0ac93ac1ff349298880a4.

~~ Specification, builders, and lifetime model ~~

SkMesh pairs a compiled SkSL vertex and fragment specification with vertex and
optional 16-bit index buffers, uniform data, and child effects, and draws only
on GPU-backed surfaces (SkBitmapDevice::drawMesh is a no-op in upstream Skia).
Earlier drafts in #3779 and #4553 coupled SKMeshBuilder.Dispose to disposing
its SKMeshSpecification, combined indexed and non-indexed state on a single
builder, and initialized uniformNames and childNames to Array.Empty<string>(),
which defeated ??= lazy enumeration and caused setting declared mesh uniforms
by name to throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

Separate specification compilation from mesh construction and align ownership
with native Skia:

  * Expose SKMeshSpecification.Create and SKMeshSpecificationBuilder
    (via new SKMeshSpecificationBuilder or SKMeshSpecification.CreateBuilder)
    with readonly struct descriptors SKMeshSpecificationAttribute and
    SKMeshSpecificationVarying, automatic attribute offset and VertexStride
    calculation, and lazy Uniforms and Children reflection integrated with
    SKRuntimeEffectUniforms and SKRuntimeEffectChildren.
  * Provide SKMeshBuilder for non-indexed meshes (via new SKMeshBuilder,
    SKMesh.CreateBuilder, or spec.CreateMeshBuilder) and derive
    SKIndexedMeshBuilder : SKMeshBuilder for indexed meshes (via
    new SKIndexedMeshBuilder, SKMesh.CreateIndexedBuilder, or
    spec.CreateIndexedMeshBuilder) with virtual/override Build() and
    Build(out string? errors) methods. Disposing a mesh builder releases its
    uniform and child collections without disposing the shared
    SKMeshSpecification.
  * Retain native references inside SkMesh across sk_mesh_make and
    sk_mesh_make_indexed so a built SKMesh remains drawable after the managed
    specification, builder, buffers, and child shaders are disposed, and
    protect P/Invoke call sites with GC.KeepAlive.

~~ Zero-allocation per-frame hot path and string marshalling ~~

Animated 3D and cloth meshes rebuild SKMesh instances every frame as vertex
counts, uniform values, or buffers change. Allocating a temporary SKData via
uniforms.ToData(), cloning children.ToArray(), allocating an SKString when
out errors is unused, or boxing SKRuntimeEffectUniformFlagsNative inside
SKRuntimeEffectUniforms.ValidateTypes adds per-frame GC pressure.

Optimize both specification creation and per-frame mesh construction:

  * Pass raw uniform pointer and byte count (fUniformData and fUniformSize)
    through SKMeshMakeArgsNative and SKMeshMakeIndexedArgsNative directly to
    native SkData::MakeWithCopy, read SKRuntimeEffectChildren.RawChildren
    without cloning the array, and allocate the error SKString only when
    captureErrors is true.
  * Replace uniform.Flags.HasFlag(SKRuntimeEffectUniformFlagsNative.Array) in
    SKRuntimeEffect.cs with a bitwise check so setting uniforms does not box
    the flags enum on non-PGO paths.
  * Add Utils.RentUtf8Strings (RentedUtf8Strings), a ref indexer on
    Utils.RentedArray<T>, and a ReadOnlySpan<SKObject> overload on
    Utils.RentHandlesArray so SKMeshSpecification.CreateCore marshals UTF-8
    attribute and varying names using pooled buffers without heap allocations.
    SKMeshBenchmark and RentedUtf8StringsBenchmark cover the per-frame builder
    reuse and UTF-8 string marshalling paths.

~~ CPU and Ganesh GPU mesh buffers ~~

Upstream Skia provides CPU-backed buffers in SkMeshes and Ganesh GPU-backed
buffers in SkMeshGanesh.h, while Graphite consumes CPU-backed mesh buffers
directly during draw recording.

Expose parameterless CPU overloads and non-nullable GRContext Ganesh overloads
for Create, Copy, and Update on SKMeshVertexBuffer and SKMeshIndexBuffer.
Enforce Skia's 4-byte size and offset alignment rules on Update in managed
code before calling into native Skia.

~~ Gallery samples and GPU rendering tests ~~

Add three interactive GPU samples in samples/Gallery/Shared/Samples
(MeshSample for a non-indexed 3D winding tunnel, MeshFlagSample for an indexed
Verlet cloth flag, and MeshGlobeSample for an indexed 3D Earth globe using the
public-domain NASA Blue Marble texture) and default the MAUI Gallery window to
GPU mode. Split the test suite into SKMeshSpecificationTest, SKMeshBufferTest,
and SKMeshTest covering validation, reference retention after wrapper
disposal, default paint color modulation, raster no-op behavior, and pixel
rendering across Ganesh OpenGL, Ganesh Metal, and Graphite Metal/Dawn.

5769.title: [Skia] Sync m159 image-filter cache equality fix
5769.body:
[Skia] Sync m159 image-filter cache equality fix (#5769)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/458
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5776
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/96ee011489be9ba83512abb766d0712a27eb1f18...1c8b6db33a5c9ff2292fb58d65d7b344e91085f3

Advance externals/skia and its Component Governance registration to native
merge 1c8b6db33a5c9ff2292fb58d65d7b344e91085f3, incorporating the
chrome/m159 cache-key fix at upstream
8a65fa27c104d1bb5a58df5ec3e0c1655053fcf6. Keep milestone 159 and package
and native ABI versions unchanged for this servicing update.

The image-filter cache hashes complete key bytes, while its former
fieldwise equality used numerical matrix comparison and ignored the
matrix's cached type mask. Signed zero, differing type-mask state and
runtime denormal handling could make equality inconsistent with hashing.
The native fix compares the complete key representation with memcmp,
using the constructor's existing type-mask initialization and explicit
padding. Its upstream regression checks signed zero, type masks,
colliding subnormal translations, LRU eviction and purge behavior.

Record the landed native history rather than the pre-merge PR head.
The native merge has two parents, directly contains reviewed commit
b57c805eedc66db3716e75ef6f5c8520be1be17b, and has the identical tree
7dbf928a42d7006783c6aaf4ae567b34f0d37824. The dependent repin updates
the gitlink and matching manifest fork hash together; the manifest's
upstream_merge_commit remains the upstream commit, not the fork merge.

The parent diff changes those two provenance files, not managed wrappers,
generated declarations or tests. Independent regeneration matched the
five maintained generator configurations, and the fork DEPS blob is
unchanged. Native tree equality preserves the reviewed content; it is
not a new native build or runtime/device test run.

5772.title: Build the docs site in parallel and validate it on every PR
5772.body:
* Build the docs site in parallel and validate it on every PR

The Pages workflow built the docs and all three WASM apps serially in one
job, and only built PRs with the automation/staging label. When the Uno 7
migration broke the Uno Gallery smoke test (#5771), nothing caught it on the
PR and every main run since has failed, so the docs stopped publishing.

Split the build into setup, docs, wasm-natives, an app matrix and a quick
assemble job. Each app uploads its output only after it builds and passes
its smoke test; assemble copies whichever apps exist and warns about any
that are missing. Every PR, including forks, now builds and smoke-tests the
site and fails on any error. Publishing still requires a same-repo PR with
automation/staging, or a push/dispatch. On main, app jobs are
continue-on-error so a broken app is omitted rather than blocking the docs.

Relates to #5771

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Separate site validation from production and preview deployment

Build every PR event, including forks and label changes. Only publish production from main or staging for explicitly labeled same-repository PRs, and require successful app builds before publishing a PR preview.\n\nGate Go Live on the upstream publishing job rather than workflow success so validation-only and dry-run builds do not redeploy Pages.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5741.title: [M159] Sync upstream glyph and Vulkan OOM fixes
5741.body:
[M159] Sync upstream glyph and Vulkan OOM fixes (#5741)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/453
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5757
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/1b7b8c4340f57877940b47d24ada18eb6ec66e68...96ee011489be9ba83512abb766d0712a27eb1f18

Advance the Skia gitlink and Component Governance registration to the landed
native merge, 96ee011489be9ba83512abb766d0712a27eb1f18, and record upstream
chrome/m159 revision 7a06b6cf9fc9fe32f8906c63da21a4e35f7e9f15.
This is a same-milestone servicing sync; package and ABI versions remain
unchanged.

The dependent repin records the actual two-parent native merge rather than
the reviewed branch head. Its tree was verified identical to reviewed commit
9f50c1175e1de5b949820c9528594ccc3fde3979, preserving the reviewed native
contents while retaining the landed merge ancestry.

~~ Mask-filtered glyph reload divergence ~~

Bring in the SkScalerContext::getImage hardening for stateful font scalers
whose successive glyph loads disagree about paths, mask formats or bounds.
The native fix rasterizes the reloaded glyph rather than stale initial
state, clears incompatible masks instead of overflowing sub-byte rows, and
uses full plane strides when copying clipped emboss masks. Regression cases
also preserve overlapping SDF data and exercise changing path geometry.

~~ Imagination Vulkan descriptor allocation failures ~~

Bring in the Ganesh and Graphite workaround for descriptor-set allocation
returning host or device OOM on Imagination drivers. The affected pool is
deliberately abandoned because destroying it can trigger a driver failure;
Graphite also refuses further allocation through the abandoned handle.
The workaround is restricted to that vendor and those allocation errors.

5700.title: Retire .NET 8 WASM and obsolete Emscripten workarounds
5700.body:
Retire .NET 8 WASM and obsolete Emscripten workarounds (#5700)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/446

Retire the .NET 8 WebAssembly toolchain while preserving the runtime-matched
archives for supported consumers. Non-WASM .NET 8 support and the existing
native Dawn integration remain unchanged.

~~ Require .NET 9 for WebAssembly native assets ~~

Remove emsdk 3.1.34 producer jobs, both artifact-merger registrations and
the corresponding native artifact inventory. Update source-build and
packaged targets for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp to reject unsupported
WASM frameworks before building.

Keep .NET 9/10 on emsdk 3.1.56 and .NET 11+ on 6.0.2, preserving threading
and SIMD selection. Newer archives are not interchangeable with older
.NET toolchains. Current package and developer documentation now describes
this support boundary; historical release records remain intact.

MSBuild coverage verifies retained archive selection, unsupported WASM
errors and unaffected non-WASM builds. Retired archive directories remain
as test decoys so their accidental selection is detectable.

~~ Use the existing modern WebGPU integration consistently ~~

The retained WASM toolchains already use emdawnwebgpu. Remove the obsolete
_SkiaSharpUseEmdawnwebgpu discriminator, built-in USE_WEBGPU linkage and
legacy mgrDevice/mgrQueue/mgrTexture fallbacks.

Continue shipping the matching port JavaScript and exporting instance
creation and texture release. Browser test interop now uses importJs*
handles directly and releases textures through wgpuTextureRelease rather
than silently accepting a missing release path.

Keep the existing native Dawn adaptations, old-toolchain JavaScript
compatibility rewrite and runtime library-order workaround. Their
requirements do not disappear with .NET 8.

~~ Remove inactive native build switches ~~

Drop SKNX_NO_SIMD, SK_DISABLE_AAA and GR_GL_CHECK_ALLOC_WITH_GET_ERROR from
the WASM build flags: the pinned native source has no tracked consumers.
SIMD selection continues through the compiler's -msimd128 flag.

The retired toolchain was also the reason for the Graphite version gate.
Graphite now follows the existing GPU setting, preserving GPU-off builds.

~~ Restore upstream PDF and SVG ranges implementations ~~

Pin mono/skia e9296dd4eb471f50a09e462f3a33bf276e5c95e4 in both the
submodule and Component Governance registration. The landed native tree
equals the reviewed tree and restores std::views::reverse in PDF structure
emission and projected std::ranges::find in SVG blend-mode selection.

Both restored translation units compile on emsdk 3.1.56 and 6.0.2 across
threading and SIMD variants. Source-built single-threaded archives link
with the retained .NET toolchains; these checks do not establish complete
browser runtime coverage.

The unfiltered managed solution passes. Browser validation has separate
documented limitations, and the unrelated Windows sample confirmation
timeout is being investigated independently rather than weakened here.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
